title: Autoimmune Bullous Disease — Diagnosis
subtitle: Decision tree: blister/erosion presentation → specific ABD

steps.prompt: Patient presents with blistering or erosive skin disorder. Are blisters/erosions present?

steps.detail: Re-evaluate for eczema, psoriasis, contact dermatitis, or other non-blistering condition. This pathway covers immunobullous disorders.

steps.prompt: What is the patient's age and clinical context?

branches.label: Adult — assess blister character and sites
Child — grouped vesicles, annular string-of-pearls pattern

steps.detail: Anti-BP180 IgG; occurs 2nd–3rd trimester or postpartum. Subepidermal blister on periumbilical urticarial plaques. DIF: linear C3 ± IgG at BMZ. Risk of neonatal blistering. Treat with superpotent topical steroids; systemic steroids if severe. Resolves postpartum but may recur with future pregnancies. PMID: 35646449.

Chronic bullous disease of childhood. IgA anti-LAD-1 (BP180 fragment). Characteristic annular 'string-of-pearls' blistering on lower trunk, perineum, face. DIF: linear IgA at BMZ. Drug trigger in adults (vancomycin is classic). First-line: dapsone; sulfapyridine if dapsone intolerant. PMID: 35646449.

branches.label: Flaccid, easily ruptured, Nikolsky positive (lateral pressure causes extension)
Tense, intact on urticarial/erythematous base, Nikolsky negative
Trauma-induced on extensor surfaces, healing with scarring + milia
Skin only — seborrheic areas (scalp, face, chest, back), scaling/crusting
Severe polymorphous mucosal lesions + known/suspected malignancy

steps.prompt: Is skin involvement present in addition to mucosa?

branches.label: Mucosal only or mucosal-dominant — minimal/no skin blisters
Both mucosa and skin extensively involved

steps.detail: Anti-Dsg3 IgG (without Dsg1). Oral mucosa often first and most severely affected. Flaccid erosions may appear before skin involvement. Intraepidermal suprabasilar split on histology. DIF: intercellular IgG + C3 in epidermis ('fishnet'). First-line: rituximab 1g ×2 (D0+D14) per PEMPHIX trial (PMID 28342637). PMID: 31498102.

Anti-Dsg3 + anti-Dsg1 IgG. Widespread flaccid blisters on skin and mucosa (oral, nasal, pharyngeal, genital, conjunctival). Suprabasilar acantholysis. DIF: intercellular IgG/C3 'fishnet'. ELISA: Dsg3 and Dsg1 positive. First-line: rituximab (PMID 28342637) ± prednisone 1–1.5 mg/kg. Steroid-sparing: azathioprine, MMF. PMID: 31498102.

Anti-Dsg1 IgG. Superficial flaccid blisters in seborrheic distribution (scalp, face, chest, back); blisters rupture rapidly leaving crusted erosions. NO mucosal involvement (Dsg3 not targeted). Subcorneal acantholysis at granular layer. DIF: intercellular IgG/C3. ELISA: Dsg1 positive, Dsg3 negative. Endemic variant: fogo selvagem (Brazil). Treatment: systemic steroids, dapsone for limited disease, rituximab/MMF for refractory. PMID: 31498102.

Severe, polymorphous mucosal erosions (often refractory) + variable skin findings (lichenoid, bullous, erythema-multiforme-like). Associated with NHL, CLL, Castleman disease, thymoma. Anti-plakins (periplakin, envoplakin), anti-Dsg3, anti-BP180. Bronchiolitis obliterans is a life-threatening complication. Action: urgent CT chest/abdomen/pelvis for malignancy. Treatment of underlying neoplasm essential; systemic steroids, rituximab. High mortality. PMID: 31498102.

steps.prompt: Older adult (>70 y)? Distribution and mucosal involvement?

branches.label: Older adult, lower trunk + flexures, no/rare mucosal involvement
Mucosal-only (oral, ocular, nasal, anogenital) with scarring tendency

steps.detail: Most common ABD. Anti-BP180 (NC16A domain) and anti-BP230 IgG; hemidesmosomal antigens. Tense blisters on urticarial, erythematous, or eczematous base. Lower trunk, inner thighs, flexures. Mucosal involvement rare. Subepidermal split. DIF: linear IgG + C3 at BMZ. Salt-split skin: epidermal (roof) pattern. ELISA: BP180 + BP230. Disease activity: BPDAI score. Drug triggers: DPP-4 inhibitors (gliptins), checkpoint inhibitors, furosemide. First-line: superpotent topical clobetasol BID (PMID 11821508 — non-inferior to oral prednisone with lower mortality). PMID: 35646449.

branches.label: Yes — ocular scarring/symblepharon present or progressing

steps.prompt: Mucous Membrane Pemphigoid — Ocular involvement (HIGH RISK)
steps.detail: Cicatricial pemphigoid with ocular involvement. Risk of corneal scarring and blindness. URGENT ophthalmology referral. Anti-laminin 332 (epiligrin) associated with increased malignancy risk — screen for cancer. Anti-BP180 also common. Requires aggressive systemic immunosuppression: cyclophosphamide + prednisone for severe ocular/laryngeal disease; rituximab for refractory. Monitor with regular ophthalmology. PMID: 35646449.

Oral mucosa (most common), nasopharynx, esophagus, anogenital. Scarring and synechiae are hallmarks distinguishing from PV. DIF: linear IgG ± IgA ± C3 at BMZ. Treatment: dapsone for mild oral; prednisone + dapsone for moderate; prednisone + cyclophosphamide or rituximab for severe. ENT and dental involvement requires co-management. PMID: 35646449.

steps.prompt: Is presentation consistent with dermatitis herpetiformis? (Pruritic grouped vesicles on extensors)

branches.label: Trauma-induced, extensor surface mechanobullous with scarring/milia
Pruritic grouped vesicles on extensors, scalp, buttocks — GI symptoms

steps.detail: Anti-Type VII collagen (sub-lamina densa anchoring fibrils). Mechanobullous (non-inflammatory) variant: trauma-induced blisters on extensor/acral sites, heals with scarring and milia. Inflammatory variant mimics BP or MMP. DIF: linear IgG at BMZ. CRITICAL: salt-split skin — dermal (floor) pattern distinguishes EBA from BP (epidermal/roof). IIF on collagen VII-deficient skin if available. Treatment: colchicine, dapsone for mild; cyclosporine, rituximab, IVIG for refractory. PMID: 35646449.

Anti-tissue transglutaminase (tTG) IgA + anti-epidermal transglutaminase (eTG) IgA. Pathognomonic: granular IgA deposits at dermal papillae tips on DIF. Associated with celiac disease (HLA-DQ2/DQ8). Intensely pruritic grouped vesicles on elbows, knees, scalp, buttocks — often so pruritic blisters are excoriated before exam. Celiac workup: anti-tTG IgA, anti-endomysial IgA, small bowel biopsy. Treatment: dapsone 50–200 mg (rapid response within 72h) + strict gluten-free diet (GFD). PMID: 35646449.
